intro.name: Welcome
intro.text: Welcome to Mudgee, in the Cudgegong River valley. The Mudgee and Dabee clans of the Wiradjuri people lived here, and the name is thought to mean something like resting place or nest in the hills, though translations vary. James Blackman was the first British colonist to enter the district, in 1821. It is the largest town in the Mid-Western Regional Council area.

stops.name: Railway station
stops.text: Mudgee railway station was designed by John Whitton and built in 1883 and 1884. Locals campaigned for a railway for nearly 25 years, and the line finally opened on 11 September 1884 with a procession, a picnic and a banquet. No trains run here now, but coaches link Lithgow and Coonabarabran.

stops.name: St Mary's Church
stops.text: St Mary's Church on Church Street was first built in 1857 and largely rebuilt between 1873 and 1876 to a design by the Bathurst architect Edward Gell. It opened on 11 November 1876, and the copper spire was added to the tower in 1911. Its organ was built in London in 1866 for a church in Randwick, and moved to Mudgee in 1907.

stops.name: Town Hall and Post Office

stops.text: Market Street has two fine civic buildings a short walk apart. The Town Hall at number 64 was built in 1880 and is now the library and theatre. The Post Office at number 80 was designed by Alexander Dawson, built in 1862 and remodelled in 1902, when the colonnade and small tower were added. Both are on the State Heritage Register.
